problem.text: GPTJ rotary style was already selectable, but its CUDA specialization contained only a TODO and wrote no rotated output.

reasoning.text: The change implements adjacent-channel rotation within the existing kernel rather than adding another positional-frequency pipeline.

impact.text: Native GPTJ calls now rotate Q and optional K; this does not register a GPT-J model architecture or complete the Torch reference implementation.

source_notes.text: The earlier modules entry identified the empty GPTJ branch and partial-rotation frequency-read concern. Inspection of this patch shows the former implemented and the latter carried over.

Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” includes util/rope.py in its import traceback. Its connection here is only an inferred file overlap: the reporter describes an environment/compiler remedy, not GPTJ rotation. The reviewed reports of incoherent low-bitrate output (#15), invalid CUDA configuration (#16), and missing torch during requirements installation (#17) do not establish motivation for this patch.

limitations: No CUDA compilation, kernel execution, model inference or performance measurement was performed.
The scalar check uses Python double precision, not CUDA fast trigonometry, float intermediates or FP16 rounding; it cannot establish device-memory behavior.

claims.text: For pair index t, GPTJ addresses channels 2t and 2t+1 and computes (u·cos−v·sin, v·cos+u·sin), with float intermediates and round-to-nearest half outputs. NEOX instead pairs t with t+partial_head_dim/2. Both modes share position selection, inverse frequencies and attention-factor scaling.

partial_head_dim is twice the inverse-frequency count. GPTJ rotates pairs below that count and copies remaining adjacent pairs using half2. The launch still uses head_dim/2 threads along x and at most 1024 threads per block, distributing Q and K heads along y with a strided loop. The NEOX copy rewrite preserves its original address arithmetic.

Named dispatch constants preserve GPTJ=1 and NEOX=2 rather than changing selection semantics. RoPE.apply makes inputs contiguous, chooses allocated or in-place outputs and forwards the configured style to ext.rope. Inspected attention callers consume its returned Q/K before SDPA or FlashAttention.

The new _rotate_half_gptj helper constructs interleaved (−odd, even) channels, but no call site is added. apply_torch still uses split-half rotation; its TODO now explicitly mentions GPTJ and partial rotary factors. Existing test parametrization enables only NEOX.

A scalar transcription checked adjacent-pair destination coverage for head/rotary dimensions 8/8, 8/4, 128/128 and 128/64. Every channel was covered once. A four-channel rotation preserved squared norm within 3.6e−15 while differing from the unchanged split-half formula.
The accompanying Hadamard edit widens the device annotation to torch.device | str without changing its conversion, scaling or caching implementation.

findings.description: The inherited unconditional frequency read remains outside the partial-rotation guard.
findings.trigger: A partial rotary frequency array shorter than head_dim/2 reaches rope_kernel.
findings.expected_behavior: Threads copying unrotated channels should not read beyond the frequency array.
findings.actual_behavior: All x threads evaluate inv_freq[t] before the rotation/copy branch. For head_dim=128 and rotary_dim=64, 32 source-level frequency indices exceed the 32-element array. Actual GPU consequences are untested.

verification.description: The parent-tree search locates ext.rope in RoPE.apply and three attention callers of self.rope.apply. Their reach is conditional on supplying partial frequencies; it is not evidence that every model uses them. The task diff leaves the shared read and launch unchanged.
verification.limits: Source-level bounds concern, not a measured CUDA fault.

verification.description: Counted launched frequency indices outside the partial array for two bounded examples.

findings.description: The Torch alternative remains incompatible with general GPTJ adjacent-pair rotation.
findings.trigger: Calling RoPE.apply_torch with GPTJ style on a four-or-more-channel head at a nontrivial angle.
findings.expected_behavior: Use adjacent even/odd channel pairs, matching the newly implemented native GPTJ path.
findings.actual_behavior: compute_sincos repeats adjacent coefficients, but the application helpers still call split-half _rotate_half rather than the newly added _rotate_half_gptj.

verification.description: Whole-parent search finds the direct apply_torch caller in tests/test_rope.py, whose active styles include only NEOX. Inspected attention paths use native apply instead.
verification.limits: External callers are not covered by repository search.

verification.description: Compared adjacent-pair and split-half formulas for [1,2,3,4] with angle 0.7; outputs differed.
verification.limits: Executed scalar formulas, not Torch or CUDA implementations.

annotation.summary: Implements native GPTJ adjacent-pair RoPE while retaining existing dispatch and position handling; the Torch alternative and partial-frequency bounds concern remain.

argv:
import math,json
checks=[]
for h,d in [(8,8),(8,4),(128,128),(128,64)]:
 writes=[j for t in range(h//2) for j in (2*t,2*t+1)]
 assert sorted(writes)==list(range(h))
 checks.append({'head_dim':h,'rotary_dim':d,'copy_channels':h-d,'frequency_indices_outside_length':sum(t>=d//2 for t in range(h//2))})
x=[1.,2.,3.,4.]; c=math.cos(.7); s=math.sin(.7)
a=[v for i in range(0,4,2) for v in (x[i]*c-x[i+1]*s,x[i+1]*c+x[i]*s)]
b=[x[i]*c+([-3.,-4.,1.,2.][i])*s for i in range(4)]
print(json.dumps({'index_checks':checks,'gptj':a,'unchanged_torch_split_half':b,'norm_error':abs(sum(v*v for v in a)-sum(v*v for v in x))}))
